claims.statement: The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott announced on 2026-08-03 a moratorium on new data centers connecting to the state grid, and ordered ERCOT to require developers to provide information on tax breaks, power use, water, community impact and ownership.
The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott directed the Texas Water Development Board on 2026-09-15 to penalize data centers that fail to report water use; only 28% had answered a mandatory survey.

The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott ordered the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality on 2026-09-21 to stop issuing environmental permits for data centers until audits are complete. No end date was given.
Data Center Watch (10a Labs), as relayed by Gizmodo, counted 75 projects worth about $130 billion blocked or delayed in Q1 2026.
Data Center Watch (10a Labs), as relayed by Gizmodo, counted 45 projects worth about $68 billion blocked or delayed from April to June 2026.

SemiAnalysis argues most projects flagged as 'canceled' are early-stage ones without site control, financing or interconnection. It says its 2026 North America hyperscaler self-build forecast moved only about 1%, and colocation under 5%, over six months.
The dcmap.us tracker lists 56 formal public actions across 25 states (22 statewide, 34 local), with entries through August 2026.
claims.source_name: dcmap.us: US Data Center Policy Tracker

claims.statement: Gallup, in a poll fielded 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-18 (1,000 adults, margin of error about 4 points), found 71% oppose construction of AI data centers in their local area and 27% favor. 48% strongly oppose.
claims.source_name: Gallup: Americans Oppose AI Data Centers in Their Area

claims.statement: The UMass Amherst Poll, fielded 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-26 (1,000 respondents, margin of error 3.5 points), found 65% oppose, 11% support and 24% neither, when asked about an AI data center in their local community.

Embold Research, for Heatmap, fielded 2026-08-08 to 2026-08-13 (2,045 registered voters, margin of error 2.3 points) and found 75% would oppose a data center built near their home, 61% strongly (per Heatmap News).
Heatmap's four polls show opposition rising from 42% (Aug 2025, with 43% in support) to 51% (Feb 2026), 70% (May 2026) and 75% (Aug 2026), per Heatmap News.

Ballotpedia counts 38 data-center-related ballot measures in eight states in 2026, including 20 in Ohio across 17 jurisdictions. 34 of the 38 are on the 2026-11-03 ballot. In the four earlier 2026 votes, voters favored greater restrictions each time.
claims.source_name: Ballotpedia News: data center ballot measures

discrepancies.description: Time News and the Texas Tribune both report Texas action on data centers. The Tribune gives dated orders: grid connections (2026-08-03), water reporting (2026-09-15) and environmental permits (2026-09-21). The governor's own orders have not yet been pulled.
discrepancies.what_would_settle_it: Governor's office press releases or executive orders; TCEQ and ERCOT notices.

discrepancies.description: Reports differ on how much capacity is really affected. Data Center Watch counts projects blocked or delayed by opposition. SemiAnalysis says most 'canceled' projects were early-stage and never had 2026 commitments. The two may count different things.
discrepancies.what_would_settle_it: Read both methodologies; compare project lists.

discrepancies.description: The polls agree on direction but differ on level. Gallup found 71% oppose and 27% favor; UMass found 65% oppose, 11% support and 24% neither. The UMass question offered a 'neither' option, which can lower measured opposition. Dates, wording and methods also differ.
discrepancies.what_would_settle_it: Compare exact questions and response options across the polls.
